records.title: A 3-Layer Agentic Model for Nonfunctional Requirements in Software Engineering
records.rationale: Position paper proposing a named three-layer (Data/Agent/Perspective) conceptual model for embedding LLM agents into nonfunctional-requirement assurance across the software lifecycle, framing both quality-of-agents and agents-for-quality. Conceptual only with illustrative examples, so it frames RQ1's verification and reliability dimension without supplying comparative evidence.

records.title: Vibe Coding vs. Agentic Coding: Fundamentals and Practical Implications of Agentic AI
records.rationale: Review contrasting human-in-the-loop prompt-driven coding against autonomous goal-driven agentic coding, with a taxonomy of execution models, feedback loops, safety mechanisms, and 20 use cases indicating where each paradigm succeeds. Provides conditions-for-autonomy framing relevant to RQ2 but compares interaction paradigms rather than single-agent versus multi-agent configurations.

records.title: Cooperative Ai Agents Using Supervised Global Workspaces
records.rationale: Describes a supervisor-governed global-workspace architecture where specialized agent personas write to a shared blackboard, reporting that strong supervision enforces orderly behaviour and diverse personas enrich dialogue. The demonstration is an e-commerce recommendation scenario with no software engineering task and no single-agent baseline, so it only illustrates supervision and persona mechanics.

records.title: Breaking the boundaries of conventional vocabulary learning: the impact of vocabulary learning with intelligent interactive companion in CAVL environments on learning outcomes, motivation, and flow experience
records.rationale: Classroom experiment on computer-assisted vocabulary acquisition where the multi-agent companion is compared against conventional courseware, not against a single LLM agent. No software engineering activity is involved, making this a pure keyword collision on 'multi-agent'.

records.title: LLM-based Satisfiability Checking of String Requirements by Consistent Data and Checker Generation
records.rationale: Empirically evaluates four LLMs on checking satisfiability of natural-language string requirements by generating SMT and Python checkers, doubling success rate and F1 over unchecked baselines. Gives concrete evidence on LLM-plus-external-verifier reliability for a requirements activity, though no agent configurations are compared.

records.title: Exploring Autonomous Agents: A Closer Look at Why They Fail When Completing Tasks
records.rationale: Builds a 34-task benchmark, measures three open-source agent frameworks across two LLM backbones at roughly 50% completion, and derives a three-tier failure taxonomy covering planning, execution, and response generation while explicitly analysing interaction and communication mechanisms. This directly answers RQ3 on what failure modes are reported and how they are measured.

records.title: A Pair Programming Framework for Code Generation via Multi-Plan Exploration and Feedback-Driven Refinement
records.rationale: PairCoder instantiates role specialization as a Navigator planner and Driver implementer and benchmarks the two-agent workflow against directly prompted single-LLM baselines across code generation benchmarks, reporting 12.00%-162.43% relative pass@1 gains. This is a direct role-specialized multi-agent versus single-agent comparison on a software engineering task, answering RQ2.

records.title: Supporting Agile Roles and Practices with GAI
records.rationale: Experience report on using an LLM as a linguistic collaborator for agile practices and roles such as Product Owner and Scrum Master, noting prompt-engineering and responsible-use challenges. The role framing is suggestive for specialization but there is no architecture, measurement, or agent configuration comparison.

records.title: Towards Multi-Agentic AI for automated software design and modelling: challenges and opportunities
records.rationale: Proposes a conceptual multi-agentic framework for design and modelling and enumerates coordination hazards including requirement ambiguity, intra- and inter-model consistency, and conflict resolution when merging design model versions. These named failure modes inform RQ3 even though no measurement or empirical study is reported.

records.title: Bot-Driven Development: From Simple Automation to Autonomous Software Development Bots
records.rationale: Vision paper and research agenda on bots taking proactive roles in coding, testing, and project management, reframing driver-navigator dynamics and raising trust, interruption, and governance questions. It offers agenda-level framing rather than any architecture, evidence, or comparison against single-agent operation.

records.title: SAGESERVE: Optimizing LLM Serving on Cloud Data Centers with Forecast Aware Auto-Scaling
records.rationale: Datacenter inference-serving work on request routing, GPU auto-scaling, and ILP-based resource allocation for Office 365 LLM workloads. There are no LLM agents and no software engineering activity being automated, only serving infrastructure economics.

records.title: LAMeD: LLM-generated Annotations for Memory Leak Detection
records.rationale: Uses an LLM to synthesize function source/sink annotations that feed static analyzers such as Cooddy, improving memory-leak detection and reducing path explosion. It is single-shot LLM tooling rather than an agentic or multi-agent configuration, so it is background on LLM-assisted defect detection.

records.title: Fuzz4All: Universal Fuzzing with Large Language Models
records.rationale: LLM-driven universal fuzzing with autoprompting and an iterative fuzzing loop that found 98 bugs across GCC, Clang, Z3, and other systems. Strong LLM4SE testing result but a single-model generation loop with no role specialization, coordination analysis, or agent-count comparison.

records.title: Prompts Engineering Challenges in Software Code Generation
records.rationale: Systematic review of 28 primary studies on prompt engineering for code generation, grouping findings into six themes and flagging prompt sensitivity, security, and over-reliance risks. It stays at the prompting layer with no agent architectures or multi-agent evidence.

records.title: AXNav: Replaying Accessibility Tests from Natural Language
records.rationale: Builds an LLM plus pixel-based UI system that executes natural-language accessibility test instructions and flags issues, validated in a 10-participant study with accessibility QA professionals. Supplies single-agent capability evidence on a realistic testing activity with unusually strong ecological validity for RQ1.

records.title: Autonomous Microscopy Experiments through Large Language Model Agents
records.rationale: AFMBench evaluates GPT-4o and GPT-3.5 agents across an experimental workflow and reports a significant performance decline specifically in multi-agent coordination scenarios plus instruction non-adherence and task divagation. The multi-agent degradation and drift evidence speaks to RQ2's underperformance conditions, but the domain is microscopy rather than software engineering.

records.title: Responsible Agentic Reasoning and AI Agents: A Critical Survey
records.rationale: Survey unifying chain-of-thought, ReAct, tool use, memory, and retrieval with responsible-AI principles, proposing an auditability-oriented evaluation protocol for agentic reasoning. It is domain-general governance framing with no software engineering tasks or agent-configuration comparison.

records.title: Intent-Driven Mobile GUI Testing with Autonomous Large Language Model Agents
records.rationale: DroidAgent is a named autonomous LLM testing agent with long- and short-term memory that reaches 61% activity coverage against 51% for state-of-the-art GUI testing baselines on the Themis benchmark. It is a measured single-agent architecture on a testing activity, useful as a single-agent reference point rather than a multi-agent comparison.

records.title: AI-Powered Commit Explorer (APCE)
records.rationale: Tool demo for storing prompts, generating commit messages, and running automated plus human evaluation of those messages. Useful tooling for an LLM4SE documentation task but it reports no comparative results, architecture claims, or coordination findings.

records.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
records.rationale: EvalPlus augments HumanEval test cases 80x and shows pass@k drops of 19.3-28.9% plus outright mis-ranking of models under insufficient tests. This is direct evidence that benchmark weakness can manufacture apparent performance differences, which bears on how single-agent versus multi-agent gains in RQ1 should be trusted.

records.title: Explaining neural scaling laws
records.rationale: Theoretical account of variance-limited and resolution-limited power-law scaling regimes for deep networks. Classic foundational citation pulled in by snowballing with no agents, no software engineering activity, and no bearing on any research question.

records.title: Large Language Models for Code Translation: An In-Depth Analysis of Code Smells and Functional Correctness
records.rationale: Large empirical study across LLMs, languages, and prompts showing code quality is largely independent of correctness, and that non-determinism exploitation, iterative repair, and LLM collaboration can each improve outcomes. The collaboration and non-determinism findings give measured signal for RQ1's performance and reliability dimensions on a translation activity.

records.title: Agentic AI-Driven CI/CD Pipelines for Autonomous Software Delivery
records.rationale: Presents a layered agentic architecture where goal statements trigger code and test agents through an adaptive CI/CD pipeline to production-ready delivery, discussing feedback loops and self-learning. It names an end-to-end multi-agent lifecycle architecture relevant to RQ1 but supplies no evaluation.

records.title: Code-DiTing: Automatic Evaluation of Code Generation without References or Test Cases
records.rationale: Empirically compares LLM-as-judge families across three datasets, characterises their accuracy, explainability, and compute trade-offs, then distills 1.5B and 7B judges that outperform far larger models and resist preference leakage. Provides verification and measurement machinery plus judge-reliability caveats relevant to RQ3's measurement question.

records.title: Meta-X design: from tools to partners in human–machine co–creation for industry 5.0
records.rationale: Industrial design framework for Industry 5.0 human-machine co-creation with a four-layer cognitive architecture. The subject is design ecosystems for physical product creation rather than LLM agents performing software engineering, and no agent configurations are compared.

records.title: Optimizing Microservice Deployment in Edge Computing with Large Language Models: Integrating Retrieval Augmented Generation and Chain of Thought Techniques
records.rationale: Uses a fine-tuned LLM with RAG and chain-of-thought decomposition to generate edge microservice deployment optimization code, reporting 22.8-39.5% latency reductions over traditional algorithms and over non-RAG prompting. The contribution is a prompting pipeline for an optimization problem rather than an agentic or multi-agent software engineering system.

records.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
records.rationale: Foundational single-agent architecture that replaces weight updates with verbal self-reflection stored in an episodic memory buffer, reaching 91% pass@1 on HumanEval with ablations over feedback signals and agent types. It defines the strong self-improving single-agent baseline that multi-agent claims in RQ2 must beat.

records.title: Toward Data Systems That Are Business Semantic Centric and AI Agents Assisted
records.rationale: Proposes BSDS, a modular data-platform blueprint combining curated business-entity data, a knowledge base for context-aware agents, and workflows aligning team expertise with business semantics. Agents are an assistive component of a data-architecture and team-organization proposal, so it is peripheral background rather than agentic software engineering evidence.
